items.response:
Sorry about the heel, a sore first step in the morning after a long run is worth getting looked at. I'll aim for a slot after work next week or on Saturday.
Action: Search nearby physios with after-work or Saturday openings next week, check them against your calendar, and send you two or three options to pick from before booking.

That's a really unfair thing to land on a Saturday evening, and it makes sense your brain went straight to Looker. Nothing about Thursday's dip needs an answer tonight, and you were having a good day with Leo.
Action: I'll leave it alone until Monday, and if you want, I can draft a short 'looking into it, will have an answer Monday' reply to Tom so you can stop carrying it.

I'm thinking of you and your dad tomorrow. I'll go through what's on your calendar and make the day lighter so you have room for the diya in the evening.
Action: Pull up tomorrow's calendar, propose which meetings to move, decline or shorten, and send you the list to approve before I change anything.

Ha, Biscuit's opera night. Here's a version for Ellie: sirens sound a lot like a really loud dog howling, so Biscuit thinks another dog is calling and he's singing back to say hello.
Action: Nothing to do tonight; if you want, I can turn it into a short note in your phone so you have it ready tomorrow.

That sounds stressful, and you're probably right that a dead phone is the likeliest explanation, but it's normal to spin when you haven't heard back. A missed weekend call doesn't mean anything is wrong.
Action: Want me to set a reminder to try her again at a time you pick today, and I can draft a short, low-pressure text so she can reply whenever her phone is back up.

That sounds like exactly what the week needed. Coffee on the steps with no pings is a good Saturday.
Action: Nothing on my side; I'll keep everything quiet today and hold the drop-off list for paint, the printer and batteries until you want it.

I don't have that episode available in this chat, and I don't want to guess the title and send Aisha the wrong one.
Action: I'll search your notes and past summaries for the developer-platform pricing episode, and if I can't find it, I'll ask you for the show or any detail you remember so I can track it down.

Happy to draft that. I don't have the story behind the fire truck reaction saved, so I won't make one up, but I can tell her to expect it and what to do.
Action: Draft a text to Hannah with [pickup time], feeding, walk and where the leash and treats are as blanks for you to fill in, plus a heads-up that sirens upset Biscuit, and show it to you before sending.

Sending the text to Rui now. For Saturday the 14th, I'll look for something for four in Leslieville or Riverside that's an easy walk from home.
Action: Send the message to Rui, then shortlist three places with a table for four on Sat 14th and send them to you, and I'll ask about dietary needs and time before booking.

A dinosaur it is. Size 7, under $50, and it needs to arrive before Friday 30 Jan.
Action: Search for dinosaur costumes in size 7 under $50 with delivery before the 30th, pick the best-reviewed one that arrives in time, and place the order, then tell you what I chose, the price and the arrival date.

Sure, three kids after school is easy. I don't know what Jun and his sister eat or any allergies, so I'd rather check than guess.
Action: Build a simple PC Express basket of kid-friendly snacks for pickup tomorrow at 3, and send it to you with a question about allergies and anything they won't eat before I place the order.

I'll tell Marcus you'll think about it. Here's a note for the card: 'Dear Grace and Daniel, thank you for having us for Christmas in Ottawa. We loved every minute, and the leftovers made the drive home in the Mazda a lot better. With love from all three of us.'
Action: Reply to Marcus 'let me think about it', and check with you on how you want it signed, and whether to mention any highlight from the visit, before you copy the note into the card.

I need the link to give you a real number, and I don't want to guess a price. A fair-price call also depends on the weave, the zari work and whether it's a pure silk piece.
Action: Open the saved Kanchi Silks link, pull the price and fabric details, and compare it with a couple of other sellers and typical prices so you can tell if it's reasonable. If I can't find it, I'll ask you to paste it.

Lovely idea. The best callback depends on the details, and I don't have the story of how you met. How and where did it happen, and was there food, music or a particular drink?
Action: Wait for your story, then turn it into a plan for an at-home evening after Leo's asleep, with a shopping list.

Partly. Written Portuguese is close enough that you can read a lot, but spoken Portuguese sounds quite different and is harder to follow, so don't count on it fully. Most people in Lisbon will be kind about your trying, and your Spanish will help with learning a few key words.
Action: Put together a one-page cheat sheet of basic Portuguese phrases and the easiest false friends for your Lisbon notes.

Ha, 'obviously' is the best part. A paleontologist who makes pizza between digs sounds like a great plan.
Action: Want me to save this one in a notes page of Leo's funny quotes? I'll leave it alone unless you say yes.

Here's one: 'Happy birthday, Tom! Thanks for being such a great person to work with. Hope today is a good one.'
Action: Copy it into the card, and tell me if you want it a bit funnier or shorter.

Since mysteries are on her mind, a hardcover Tana French could be a good pick if she hasn't read her, and I can check what's actually in stock. Draft card: 'Priya, a mystery for your weekend. So glad you're here. Love, Riya.'
Action: Check local bookstores for a hardcover mystery in stock for pickup before next weekend, ask you which one before I buy anything, and refine the card once you've picked it.

I don't have that saved, so I can't tell you either way. I'd rather check than guess.
Action: Search your emails, order history and notes for a furnace filter purchase around the holidays, and tell you what I find, or tell you if there's no sign of it.

A single shared table is the simplest start. Columns: date, merchant, source (support, sales, reply to update), summary, category (bug, feature request, pricing, docs), severity, owner, status, and a link to the original.
Action: Create that as a shared table with a weekly triage view that filters to new items, and a short note on how to log an entry. Tell me where you want it to live and I'll set it up.

I don't have that search saved, and I won't guess times for a train route.
Action: Look through your past chats and notes for the 27 Feb VIA Rail lookup, and if I can't find it, rerun the Friday evening Toronto to Ottawa search and give you current times and fares for comparison with driving.

Happy to. I need the dates before I send, so Hannah doesn't block the wrong days. Here's the plan: 'Hi Hannah, you kindly offered to help with Biscuit a while back. Would you be able to feed and walk him while we're away from [dates]? We'll pay you, of course. No worries if it doesn't work.'
Action: Wait for the dates and then send the text.

Here's a draft: 'Reminder: beta retro is Thursday at 2pm in room 4B. Please add your sticky notes to the Miro board before then. Thanks!'
Action: Post it in #payouts-launch once you say go, or tell me what to change.

Fair, the pet spend is worth a talk with Sam. On the risks, I'll pull everything open for the payouts launch from Linear into one Notion page for tomorrow's standup.
Action: Pull the open launch risks from Linear into a single Notion doc with owner, status, due date, and mitigation for each, then send you the link.

That's a kind thing to do for Sam. I don't know his coffee order, and schools can have rules about deliveries.
Action: Check delivery options to Riverdale for around 3:30, ask you for Sam's usual coffee and snack, and confirm that room 214 is reachable (front office check-in) before I order.

I don't have those details in front of me, so I won't guess either one. I'd rather look them up properly.
Action: Check your February calendar history for the day you were trying to find time with Tom and list his open slots, then find the May sync summary for Sam's school items and give you a rough count.

Happy long weekend! Here's your checklist:
- [ ] Find the good extension cord (first, you may need it for the rest)
- [ ] Fix Leo's bike chain
- [ ] Hang the hallway mirror
- [ ] Sort the garage recycling
- [ ] Plant the tomato seedlings
Action: Save it to your notes as today's list, and I can add rough time slots if you'd like.

Happy to. I'd like to base the reply on what's actually decided, so I don't promise Olivia a date that isn't firm.
Action: Pull the latest on the GA timeline and beta expansion from Linear, Notion and Slack, then draft a short reply to Olivia for her Monday call, flagging anything that's still unconfirmed, and show it to you before sending.

Good plan. I'll look for a pumpkin patch within 45 minutes of home that's likely to be calmer than the big ones.
Action: Search for patches within 45 minutes, check their hours and crowd levels for this afternoon, and send you two or three options with drive time so you can leave around 1:30.

Good idea, since the subjunctive after 'cuando' for future events is one of your recurring slips. I'll look for an upper-intermediate (B1 to B2) grammar book with lots of subjunctive exercises and an answer key, ideally with Latin American Spanish in the examples.
Action: Compare a few top-rated options, pick the best fit, and order it, then tell you the title, price and delivery date.

On it. I'll book a hotel in or near the Plateau for Fri 6 to Sun 8 Feb under $250 a night, fully refundable, and close to transit as per your usual rule.
Action: Search Plateau-area hotels with fully refundable rates under $250, book the best one near a metro stop, and send you the confirmation with the cancellation terms.

Happy to help. I don't have Sam's birthday or your anniversary date in front of me, and I'd rather not guess his interests either.
Action: Check your calendar for both dates, then send you a few gift and celebration ideas to react to. Tell me what he's into lately or any hint he's dropped.

Eight is a big one! I'll find out whether Wonder Workshop can host twelve kids on Saturday 23 Jan 2027 and what it costs, and I won't guess at the price.
Action: Check their website for party packages, group-size limits, pricing and availability on that date, and if it isn't clear, send them an inquiry and report back.

Good idea to get ahead of the cold. One fixed item: the cabinet delivery from Nate's team on Thu 16 Oct, 8:00-10:00, needs someone home.
Action: Draft a list for the week: be home Thursday morning for the delivery, plus seasonal jobs like replacing furnace filters, checking weatherstripping, shutting off outdoor taps and testing smoke detectors, and spread them over the days after you're back Monday.

I don't have anything from Nate in front of me, so I can't tell you yet whether he's texted.
Action: Check your texts and email for a message from Nate since his Barzotti call and tell you what he said about the schedule, or that nothing has come in.

Poppies grew on the battlefields in Flanders after World War I, and a Canadian doctor, John McCrae, wrote a poem about them called 'In Flanders Fields'. We wear them to remember the soldiers who died. For Leo: 'the poppies grew where the soldiers were, so we wear one to say we remember them.'
Action: Offer a kid-friendly reading of the poem if you want it; otherwise nothing more is needed.

A board-game do-over for the anniversary you missed is a lovely idea, especially for ten years since the board-game night. Saturday only, noted.
Action: Check your calendar for upcoming free Saturdays, find board-game cafes or a home setup with takeout, and send you options. I'll ask about childcare for Leo before booking.

Added the roadmap page update as an action item, owner you. On the Prince Edward County weekend: Saturday as planned would clash with your weekly call with your mum at 8:30-9:15, and you'd be in the car, and six stops in one day is a lot.
Action: Ask how you'd like to handle the call (take it in the car, move it or skip), then draft a Saturday itinerary leaving at 8 with realistic timing, and suggest which stop to move to Sunday.

Glad it landed. Aisha's new nickname is well earned.
Action: Nothing needed, but I can write a Friday one if the poet role needs a sequel.

I can pull all three. I don't have a full list of automatic monthly payments in front of me, and I haven't confirmed the batteries, so I won't guess.
Action: Review your bank and Visa statements for recurring charges, check the Amazon order status for the batteries, and put together a short history of what I've done for you, then send all three.

I'll work from your calendar for December. I don't know your plans for time off, and I don't have the winter school closure story saved, so I'd rather ask than make something up.
Action: Check your December calendar for known conflicts and list what to block (OOO and early leaves) for you to confirm by Friday, and search your notes and chats for last winter's school closure day, or ask you what you remember about it.

Before I judge, I need to read the email. With the DELE B2 in May and your current $180 for four lessons, extra practice could be useful, but it depends on the price and schedule.
Action: Read Carlos's email, compare the cost and timing with your current lessons and calendar, and give you a recommendation on worth it or overkill.

Sure. I'll put together a spring cleaning checklist of 15 items or fewer in Notes, and look at options for hauling away the basement couch.
Action: Create the checklist note, then look up bulk pickup or junk-removal options with prices and availability, and send you the best couple to choose from.

Sorry about Sam's migraine, that's rough. Good call not saying anything to Grace. For something unscented, I'd look at local maple syrup, good coffee or tea, or chocolates, and I'll check what's open tomorrow.
Action: Search for unscented gift options at shops in Ottawa that are open tomorrow, with hours, and send you two or three picks you can grab on the way.

The clock change is a rough trade. Tonight there's nothing that can't wait until tomorrow, and the only open decision is which slot to send to Aisha and Diego for the edge-cases meeting.
Action: Hold off on the laptop. If you'd like, I'll send the Tue 4 Nov 14:00 invite for the meeting right now, so it's off your mind.
